newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-British Biotech drugs nearing market.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-British Biotech drugs nearing market.

text.p: British Biotech Plc reported slightly wider first-quarter losses on Wednesday, but the leading drug development company said it was on target to bring its very first products to the market.

The Oxford-based group, which is seen as a bellwether for Britain's biotech industry, posted losses of 8.0 million pounds ($12.47 million) in the three months to July compared with 7.0 million pounds a year before.

Much more important news of progress on its pipeline, which includes the potential multi-billion dollar anti-cancer therapy Marimastat, was not greeted with the wild excitement that marked previous statements from the company, which has seen its shares soar as high as 350 pence over the past year.
The stock was trading one penny higher at 205 pence todards the end of trade.
But analysts took comfort from confident statements about acute pancreatitis drug Lexipafant, which British Biotech said could be submitted for approval in early 1997 and be on sale a year later.
Even more encouraging for analysts was news that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved the start of late-stage trials of Marimastat in four additional cancers.
Phase III tests are already underway in pancreatic cancer, a condition described by one analyst as "pretty much a death sentence".
This helped offset disappointment over drugs giant Glaxo Wellcome Plc's decision to abandon work on a British Biotech asthma pill because of lack of efficacy.
"I don't think you'd find one in a hundred investors who'd invested in us on the strength of that," finance director James Noble told Reuters in an interview.
Noble said the company's energies were now dedicated to Lexipafant and Marimastat. "Everything else is much more of a sideshow. They are the nearest to market."

Investors will have more to chew on in November, when results of late-stage trials of Lexipafant will be published. British Biotech's brokers, ABN Amro Hoare Govett, predict peak turnover of 300 million pounds a year for the drug.
Raw data on Marimastat, including analysis of its effectiveness in stomach, colo-rectal, ovarian and pancreatic cancer, will be presented to the European Society of Medical Oncology the same month.
Noble hopes to tie-up a Japanese partnership on Marimastat before the end of 1996. Hoare Govett predicts peak sales of 4.6 billion pounds for the drug. "That's looking very good," Noble said.

The company ended the first quarter with cash reserves of 200 million pounds. Noble said spending in the year to April would rise sharply to around 40 million pounds as it moves drugs towards the market, builds new laboratories and consolidates operations on a single site.

British Biotech was one of many biotech companies to go to the market for cash this year. A controversial rights issue in July raise 143 million pounds but coincided with a bout of nerves among biotech investors and sharp falls in share prices.

"What we have seen this year is a tremendous amount of money being raised and perhaps there is a bit of fatigue," Noble said. "The next phase is data from the companies proving that they are worth investing in." $1=.6415 Pound)
